newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Potato starch tax class depends on acetyl content - Court.
newsitem.headline: Potato starch tax class depends on acetyl content - Court.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday the customs classification for esterified potato starch depends on its acetyl content.
The court left to national courts to determine whether the potato starch has been altered by the process of esterification to such a high degree that it is no longer native potato starch.
A maximum acetyl content between 0.61 percent and 0.74 percent by weight does not automatically remove potato starch from the Common Customs Tariff for starches or inulin, the court said.
Joined Cases C-274/95, C-275/95 and C-276/95

on the interpretation of Common Customs Tariff as laid down in Coumcil regulation (EEC) No 3618/86 of 24 November 1986, as amended, and of Combined Nomenclature as contained in Council regulation (EEC) No 2658/87 on the tariff and statistical nomenclature and on the Common Customs Tariff (OJ 1987 L 256. p. 1)

1. The classification of esterified potato starch under heading 11.08A IV of Council regulation (EEC) No 3618/86 of 24 November 1986, as amended, and under subheading 1108 13 00 of the Combined Nomenclature as contained in Council regulation (EEC) No 2658/87 on the tariff and statistical nomenclature and on the Common Customs Tariff (and under subheading 3505 10 50 of the Combined Nomenclature) is primarily dependent on its acetyl content and thus on its degree of esterificiation. Nevertheless, it is for the national court to determine whether the nature of the esterification does not amount to an alteration of the potato starch such that it no longer corresponds qualitatively to native potato starch.

2. A maximum acetyl content of between 0.61 percent and 0.74 percent by weight of esterified potato starch does not preclude its being classified under heading 11.08A IV of the Common Customs Tariff and under subheading 1108 13 00 of the Combined Nomenclature.
